description:
- The task: design a **Solopreneur view** for `/solopreneur`, delivered as a document covering structure, components, functionalities, and implementation.
- Explored the Vue 3 + vue-router + Vuex + Tailwind codebase and found no existing "solopreneur" code, so it's a greenfield feature.
- Produced a first proposal (new store + API module + route + components), then revised it per the user's reuse-first requirement: **no new endpoints or store module** — reuse/extend existing stores, APIs, and components, creating new ones only for exclusive Solopreneur functionality.
- Identified key implementation risks, including the `store/project.js` project-restore guard misreading `/solopreneur` as a project name and redirecting home.
- Final deliverable: a developer-facing document (`wiki/solopreneur-view.md`) with the full component set, reuse mapping, routing, shell handling, and implementation plan.

messages.content:
We need a solopreneur view. It will be used for solopreneur mode defined by /solopreneur route path.

Find attached the mockups. Analyze and create a document with the structure, components, funcionalities and a proposal for implementation.

I'll start by exploring the project structure and looking for existing patterns related to routing and views.Let me examine the routing, view management, and app registration patterns in more detail.Let me search more thoroughly for any existing "solopreneur" references and check the project documentation.Let me examine the top-level app layout and a couple of full-screen views to ground the implementation proposal.Let me look at the store registration and API module patterns to make the implementation proposal concrete.Let me verify how API modules are wired into the main API object.I have enough context now. Here's my analysis and the resulting design document.

## 1. Review & Understand the Task

- Add a **Solopreneur view** to `codx-junior-ui`, reachable at the top-level route **`/solopreneur`**.
- Deliverable: a single document covering **structure**, **components**, **functionalities**, and an **implementation proposal** that fits the existing codebase.

## 2. Information Gathering — key findings

- **Stack**: Vue 3 + `vue-router` + Vuex (`typed-vuex`) + Tailwind/DaisyUI.
- **Routing** (`src/router/index.ts`): all product routes are project-scoped (`/:projectName/...`), auto-prefixed via `withProject()`. A top-level `/solopreneur` route is a static segment and would naturally match before the dynamic `/:projectName` route. There is already precedent for an unscoped screen (`/shared`).
- **App registry** (`src/config/apps.js` + `src/config/appComponentsMap.js`): apps are declared once and opened either as desktop dockview panels or as mobile/routes via `$ui.openApp`.
- **Shell** (`src/App.vue`): renders `DesktopSidebar` + `<RouterView/>`. A "mode" that needs a full-screen (sidebar-less) experience needs a small shell condition.
- **Store** (`src/store/index.js`, `typed-vuex` modules) and **API modules** (`src/api/modules/*.js`, lazy getters in `src/api/api.js`) have clean, copy-paste patterns to follow.
- **Reference full-screen view**: `src/views/TeamView.vue` is the best template (header + stats strip + toolbar + scrollable content + modals/drawers).
- No existing "solopreneur" references anywhere in the repo — this is greenfield.

## 3. Change Proposal

Create a **Solopreneur mode** as a top-level, full-screen route with:

1. A route entry + view shell (`/solopreneur`).
2. A small set of components under `src/components/solopreneur/`.
3. A `solopreneur` Vuex module + a `solopreneur` API module (endpoint contract included so the backend can be built in parallel).
4. Wiring in `apps.js`, `appComponentsMap.js`, `store/index.js`, `api/api.js`, and a minimal `App.vue` shell condition.

The document below captures all of this. One thing to note: I can infer the *structure* of the three mockups from the product domain, but I cannot pixel-read the attached images, so I've marked interpretation-sensitive details explicitly and kept the design data-driven so labels/ordering are trivial to adjust.

# Solopreneur View — Structure, Components, Functionalities & Implementation Proposal

**Status:** Design proposal (awaiting validation against the attached mockups)
**Route:** `/solopreneur`
**Related feature:** Solopreneur mode

> **Note on mockup interpretation.** The three mockups describe the Solopreneur
> experience as three screens. The analysis below captures the recurring
> building blocks across those screens. Where the mockups are ambiguous (exact
> labels, ordering, copy, colors) the document marks it as an *assumption* and
> keeps the design **data-driven** so those details can be adjusted without
> touching the component structure.

---

## Table of contents

1. [Objective](#1-objective)
2. [Context — where Solopreneur mode fits](#2-context--where-solopreneur-mode-fits)
3. [Mockup analysis](#3-mockup-analysis)
4. [Information architecture & layout](#4-information-architecture--layout)
5. [Components](#5-components)
6. [Functionalities](#6-functionalities)
7. [Data model & state](#7-data-model--state)
8. [API integration](#8-api-integration)
9. [Implementation proposal](#9-implementation-proposal)
10. [Open questions & assumptions](#10-open-questions--assumptions)

---

## 1. Objective

Give a **solo founder** a focused, single-user workspace that:

- Lives at the top-level route **`/solopreneur`** (not project-scoped).
- Presents a **command-center dashboard** that consolidates the venture's
  goals, tasks, knowledge, activity and metrics in one screen.
- Centers on an **AI assistant** ("co-founder") as the primary interaction
  surface.
- Reuses existing codx-junior building blocks (chats, tasks, knowledge,
  metrics) instead of reimplementing them.

Acceptance criteria:

- Navigating to `/solopreneur` renders the Solopreneur view.
- The view works on desktop **and** mobile (single-mode behavior).
- The three screens shown in the mockups are covered by the component set below.
- The implementation follows the existing router/app/store/API patterns.

---

## 2. Context — where Solopreneur mode fits

codx-junior already has two *view modes* (`src/store/ui.js` → `viewMode`):

| Mode | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `vibe` | Focused, one-task-at-a-time coding workspace. |
| `expert` | Full desktop workspace with dockview panels. |

**Solopreneur mode** is a third, *role-shaped* surface. It is not a `viewMode`
toggle inside a project; it is a **standalone route** that re-frames the product
around a solo operator instead of a developer team.

Key differences from the existing expert experience:

- **Top-level route** — no `/:projectName` prefix.
- **Single-user focus** — hides team/collaboration affordances.
- **Business framing** — goals, roadmap, content, growth instead of boards/PRs.
- **AI-first** — the assistant is a first-class, always-visible element.

---

## 3. Mockup analysis

The three mockups are interpreted as:

| # | Screen (assumed) | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **Command Center / Dashboard** | Landing screen: venture header, KPIs, quick actions, AI assistant prompt, recent activity. |
| 2 | **Module view** | A structured module (e.g. *Goals/OKRs*, *Roadmap*, *Tasks*) as a filterable list/grid with per-item AI actions. |
| 3 | **Item detail / wizard** | A detail panel or step-by-step wizard for creating/editing one item (goal, task, or content piece). |

The recurring building blocks across all three screens are:

1. **Top header bar** — venture identity, primary action, mode controls.
2. **Metric / KPI strip** — compact stat chips.
3. **AI assistant surface** — a prompt box with AI-generated responses.
4. **Content list/grid** — a repeatable card list, filterable and searchable.
5. **Detail/editor** — a drawer or modal for a single item.
6. **Wizard** — optional step-by-step flow for structured creation.

> **Assumption to validate:** the exact module names (Goals, Roadmap, Content,
> etc.) and their labels are inferred. The component model below treats modules
> as *config*, so adding/renaming a module does not require new components.

---

## 4. Information architecture & layout

### 4.1 Route & navigation

```txt
/solopreneur                     → SolopreneurView (dashboard)
/solopreneur/:module             → SolopreneurView, focused module
/solopreneur/:module/:itemId     → SolopreneurView, item detail open
```

- `/solopreneur` is a **static top-level route**; Vue Router ranks it above the
  dynamic `/:projectName` route, so no conflict.
- It must be excluded from the project-prefix injection (it is — that helper
  only targets routes containing `:projectName`).
- Internal navigation between dashboard ↔ module ↔ item uses router state so
  deep-links and back-navigation work.

### 4.2 Screen layout (desktop)

```txt
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ SolopreneurHeader                                            │
│ [Venture identity]        [actions] [mode/toggle]            │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ SolopreneurMetrics (KPI strip)                               │
├───────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┤
│                               │                              │
│  SolopreneurModuleList /      │  SolopreneurAssistant        │
│  SolopreneurDashboard         │  (AI co-founder panel)       │
│  (scrollable)                 │  (sticky)                    │
│                               │                              │
└───────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────┘
```

On mobile the assistant collapses into a bottom sheet / floating action button.

### 4.3 Module registry (data-driven)

Modules are described by a config array, not by bespoke components:

```js
// src/components/solopreneur/modules.js (illustrative)
export const SOLOPRENEUR_MODULES = [
  { id: 'goals',    title: 'Goals',        icon: 'fa-solid fa-bullseye',    description: '…' },
  { id: 'roadmap',  title: 'Roadmap',      icon: 'fa-solid fa-map',          description: '…' },
  { id: 'tasks',    title: 'Tasks',        icon: 'fa-brands fa-trello',      description: '…' },
  { id: 'content',  title: 'Content',      icon: 'fa-regular fa-pen-to-square', description: '…' },
  { id: 'growth',   title: 'Growth',       icon: 'fa-solid fa-arrow-trend-up', description: '…' }
]
```

This mirrors the existing `src/config/apps.js` philosophy: one registry, one
renderer.

---

## 5. Components

Proposed folder: `src/components/solopreneur/` and one view in `src/views/`.

| Component | Responsibility | Key props / events |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `views/SolopreneurView.vue` | Route component; owns layout + active module/state; delegates to sub-components. | `params`, reads `$route` |
| `SolopreneurHeader.vue` | Venture name/icon, primary action, module nav/toggle, reload. | `venture`, emits `navigate`, `create`, `reload` |
| `SolopreneurMetrics.vue` | KPI/stat chips strip. | `metrics: [{label, value, icon, tone}]` |
| `SolopreneurDashboard.vue` | Dashboard grid: quick actions + module cards + recent activity. | `venture`, `activity`, `modules` |
| `SolopreneurAssistant.vue` | AI prompt box + streamed responses + suggestion chips. | `venture`, emits `send`, `select-suggestion` |
| `SolopreneurModuleList.vue` | Searchable/filterable list+grid of a module's items. | `module`, `items`, emits `select`, `create` |
| `SolopreneurItemCard.vue` | Single item card (title, status, due date, tags, AI actions). | `item`, emits `open`, `run` |
| `SolopreneurItemDetail.vue` | Drawer/modal for viewing/editing one item. | `item`, emits `save`, `close`, `delete` |
| `SolopreneurWizard.vue` | Step-by-step structured creation flow. | `steps`, emits `submit`, `cancel` |
| `SolopreneurEmptyState.vue` | Empty/loading/error states (reusable). | `type`, `message` |

Reference implementation to copy structural conventions from:
`src/views/TeamView.vue` (header → stats → toolbar → content → modals).

---

## 6. Functionalities

### 6.1 Command Center (screen 1)

- Show **venture identity** (name, tagline, icon).
- Show **KPI metrics** (e.g. active goals, open tasks, content scheduled,
  growth score — *exact KPIs are config-driven*).
- Provide **quick actions** (create goal, create task, ask AI, open module).
- Surface **recent activity** (latest AI actions, completed items).
- Keep the **AI assistant** visible for a natural-language command.

### 6.2 Module view (screen 2)

- List items for the active module in **list** and **grid** views.
- **Search** and **filter** (status, tags, date).
- Per-item **AI actions** (generate, expand, summarize, execute).
- **Create / edit / delete** items with confirmation.

### 6.3 Item detail & wizard (screen 3)

- Open an item in a **drawer/modal** without leaving the module.
- **Wizard** flow for structured creation (name → description → attributes →
  review).
- Persist through the store; reflect immediately in the list.

### 6.4 Cross-cutting

- **AI assistant** is reusable across all three screens.
- **Responsive**: desktop two-column, mobile stacked with bottom assistant.
- **Loading / empty / error** states on every data region.
- **Notifications** via the existing `$ui.addNotification`.

---

## 7. Data model & state

New Vuex module `src/store/solopreneur.js` (typed-vuex, `namespaced: true`),
registered in `src/store/index.js`.

```js
export const state = () => ({
  venture: null,          // { id, name, tagline, icon }
  modules: [],            // module registry snapshot
  activeModuleId: null,
  items: {},              // moduleId -> items[]
  metrics: [],
  activity: [],
  loading: false,
  error: null,
  assistant: {
    busy: false,
    history: []           // [{ role, content, ts }]
  }
})
```

Actions (illustrative):

```js
export const actions = actionTree({ state, getters, mutations }, {
  async load({ commit }) { /* venture + modules + metrics + activity */ },
  async loadModule({ commit }, moduleId) { /* items for one module */ },
  async createItem({ commit }, { moduleId, payload }) { /* POST, then reload */ },
  async updateItem({ commit }, { moduleId, item }) {},
  async deleteItem({ commit }, { moduleId, itemId }) {},
  async askAssistant({ commit }, message) { /* POST, stream into history */ }
})
```

Persistence rule: the **API is the single source of truth** — same convention
as `TeamView.vue`, which re-reads after every mutation.

---

## 8. API integration

New module `src/api/modules/solopreneur.js`, exported as a factory and wired
with a lazy getter in `src/api/api.js` (same as `infraModule`).

```js
export function solopreneurModule(API) {
  const get = p => API.get(p)
  const post = (p, b) => API.post(p, b)
  const put = (p, b) => API.put(p, b)
  const del = p => API.delete(p)
  const slug = id => encodeURIComponent(id)

  return {
    endpoints: SOLOPRENEUR_ENDPOINTS,
    venture: () => get('/api/solopreneur/venture'),
    modules: () => get('/api/solopreneur/modules'),
    items: (moduleId) => get('/api/solopreneur/modules/' + slug(moduleId) + '/items'),
    createItem: (moduleId, payload) => post('/api/solopreneur/modules/' + slug(moduleId) + '/items', payload),
    updateItem: (moduleId, itemId, payload) => put('/api/solopreneur/modules/' + slug(moduleId) + '/items/' + slug(itemId), payload),
    deleteItem: (moduleId, itemId) => del('/api/solopreneur/modules/' + slug(moduleId) + '/items/' + slug(itemId)),
    metrics: () => get('/api/solopreneur/metrics'),
    activity: () => get('/api/solopreneur/activity'),
    ask: (message) => post('/api/solopreneur/assistant', { message })
  }
}
```

Ship the endpoint contract to the backend as a machine-readable array, exactly
like `INFRA_ENDPOINTS` in `src/api/modules/infra.js`:

```js
export const SOLOPRENEUR_ENDPOINTS = [
  { method: 'GET',  path: '/api/solopreneur/venture',                     desc: 'Venture profile.', response: 'SolopreneurVenture' },
  { method: 'GET',  path: '/api/solopreneur/modules',                      desc: 'Module catalog.', response: '{ modules: [] }' },
  { method: 'GET',  path: '/api/solopreneur/modules/:moduleId/items',      desc: 'Items in a module.', response: '{ items: [] }' },
  { method: 'POST', path: '/api/solopreneur/modules/:moduleId/items',      desc: 'Create an item.', body: 'SolopreneurItem', response: 'SolopreneurItem' },
  { method: 'PUT',  path: '/api/solopreneur/modules/:moduleId/items/:id',  desc: 'Update an item.', body: 'SolopreneurItem', response: 'SolopreneurItem' },
  { method: 'DELETE', path: '/api/solopreneur/modules/:moduleId/items/:id', desc: 'Delete an item.', response: '{ ok: true }' },
  { method: 'GET',  path: '/api/solopreneur/metrics',                      desc: 'KPI strip values.', response: '{ metrics: [] }' },
  { method: 'GET',  path: '/api/solopreneur/activity',                     desc: 'Recent activity feed.', response: '{ activity: [] }' },
  { method: 'POST', path: '/api/solopreneur/assistant',                    desc: 'Ask the AI assistant.', body: '{ message }', response: 'AssistantReply' }
]
```

> **Assumption to validate:** the backend endpoints above are proposed. Until
> the backend lands, the module can fall back to local/mock data (the codebase
> already uses this approach — see the `infra` module's "mock-backed" note).

---

## 9. Implementation proposal

### 9.1 Files to create

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `src/views/SolopreneurView.vue` | Route component / full-screen shell. |
| `src/components/solopreneur/modules.js` | Module registry (data-driven). |
| `src/components/solopreneur/SolopreneurHeader.vue` | Header bar. |
| `src/components/solopreneur/SolopreneurMetrics.vue` | KPI strip. |
| `src/components/solopreneur/SolopreneurDashboard.vue` | Dashboard content. |
| `src/components/solopreneur/SolopreneurAssistant.vue` | AI assistant panel. |
| `src/components/solopreneur/SolopreneurModuleList.vue` | Module list/grid. |
| `src/components/solopreneur/SolopreneurItemCard.vue` | Item card. |
| `src/components/solopreneur/SolopreneurItemDetail.vue` | Item detail drawer/modal. |
| `src/components/solopreneur/SolopreneurWizard.vue` | Step wizard. |
| `src/components/solopreneur/SolopreneurEmptyState.vue` | Loading/empty/error state. |
| `src/store/solopreneur.js` | Vuex module. |
| `src/api/modules/solopreneur.js` | API client + endpoint contract. |

### 9.2 Files to modify

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `src/router/index.ts` | Add the `/solopreneur` route (before the catch-all). |
| `src/config/apps.js` | Optional: register `solopreneur` as an app entry. |
| `src/config/appComponentsMap.js` | Map `solopreneur` → `SolopreneurView`. |
| `src/store/index.js` | Import + register the `solopreneur` module. |
| `src/api/api.js` | Import module + add lazy `get solopreneur()` getter. |
| `src/App.vue` | Hide the standard sidebar for `/solopreneur` (full-screen mode). |

### 9.3 Route change (`src/router/index.ts`)

```ts
import SolopreneurView from '@/views/SolopreneurView.vue'

// Inside routes, BEFORE the catch-all:
{
  path: '/solopreneur',
  name: 'solopreneur',
  component: SolopreneurView
},
{
  path: '/solopreneur/:module',
  name: 'solopreneur-module',
  component: SolopreneurView
},
{
  path: '/solopreneur/:module/:itemId',
  name: 'solopreneur-item',
  component: SolopreneurView
}
```

Because these routes are **not** `/:projectName`-prefixed, the `withProject()`
helper in `router/index.ts` will not touch them.

### 9.4 Store registration (`src/store/index.js`)

```js
import * as solopreneur from './solopreneur'

const modules = {
  // …existing…
  solopreneur
}
```

### 9.5 API registration (`src/api/api.js`)

```js
import { solopreneurModule } from './modules/solopreneur'

// Inside the API object:
get solopreneur() {
  if (!API._solopreneurModule) {
    API._solopreneurModule = solopreneurModule(API)
  }
  return API._solopreneurModule
}
```

### 9.6 Shell handling (`src/App.vue`)

Add a computed flag and gate the sidebar:

```js
computed: {
  isSolopreneur() {
    return this.$route?.name === 'solopreneur'
      || this.$route?.name === 'solopreneur-module'
      || this.$route?.name === 'solopreneur-item'
  }
}
```

```html
<DesktopSidebar v-if="isDesktopLandscape && !isSolopreneur" … />
```

### 9.7 Suggested build order

1. **Router + empty view** — `/solopreneur` renders `SolopreneurView`.
2. **Store + API module** — state shape and endpoint contract first.
3. **Header + Metrics + Dashboard** — screen 1.
4. **ModuleList + ItemCard** — screen 2.
5. **ItemDetail + Wizard** — screen 3.
6. **Assistant** — wire to chat/agent APIs.
7. **Responsive pass + App.vue shell handling**.

---

## 10. Open questions & assumptions

These need confirmation before (or early in) implementation:

1. **Mockup specifics** — exact module names, labels, KPI definitions and the
   third screen's exact purpose should be confirmed. The design above is
   intentionally config-driven so these are cheap to correct.
2. **Project scoping** — `/solopreneur` is top-level (per the request). Should
   the view internally select a *default venture/project*, or manage its own
   venture entity independent of `projects`?
3. **Shell** — should `/solopreneur` be a true full-screen mode (no standard
   `DesktopSidebar`), or live inside the existing shell? Proposed: full-screen.
4. **AI assistant backing** — should it reuse the existing `chats`/agent APIs
   (recommended) or introduce a bespoke `/api/solopreneur/assistant`?
5. **Persistence** — is venture data project-scoped (existing backend) or a new
   top-level store?
6. **Mobile** — confirm the assistant should become a bottom sheet rather than a
   sticky right rail.

---

*Reference for patterns used in this proposal:*
`src/router/index.ts`, `src/config/apps.js`, `src/config/appComponentsMap.js`,
`src/store/index.js`, `src/store/ui.js`, `src/store/views.js`,
`src/api/api.js`, `src/api/modules/infra.js`, `src/views/TeamView.vue`.
</file_change>

# codx-junior UI — Features & Functionality Guide

**codx-junior** is an AI-powered development workspace. It brings your projects,
chats with AI assistants, task boards, documentation, knowledge search, code
review, team collaboration and analytics together in a single application.

This guide is written **for end users**. It explains *what you can do* and *why
it matters*, grouped by topic. No technical or installation details are covered
here — only the features you will see and use.

codx-junior adapts to the device you are using and gives you two ways to work:

- **Desktop mode** — a flexible workspace where several apps stay open at the
  same time as side-by-side **panels** (like windows).
- **Single mode** — a focused, one-app-at-a-time experience used on smaller
  screens and mobile.

### The sidebar

The left sidebar is your main launcher. It gives quick access to your projects,
recent chats, tasks and the most used apps.

- **Collapse / expand** the sidebar to gain screen space.
- On **mobile** the sidebar slides in as an overlay and closes automatically when
  you navigate away.

### Main menu & command palette

- The **Menu** button opens the full application menu (projects, views,
  workspaces, settings and every app).
- **Top bar search / command palette** (shortcut **⌘K**) lets you jump straight
  to a project, chat or command without hunting through menus.

> **Tip:** In desktop mode you can open the same app several times (for example,
> one Task Manager per board) and arrange them however you like. In single mode,
> opening an app replaces the current one.

---

## Projects

A **project** is the unit everything else revolves around — chats, tasks,
knowledge, wiki and analytics all belong to a project.

### Working with multiple projects

- **Switch projects** at any time from the project selector, sidebar or menu.
- The address bar always reflects which project you are working in, so you can
  bookmark or refresh a page and stay in the same project.
- **Recent projects** are remembered, and you can **pin** your favourite projects
  for one-click switching.

### Project structure

- Projects can be **nested**: a project can have **sub-projects** and a
  **parent project**.
- **Linked / dependency projects** can be associated so the AI can search and
  reference related work across projects.
- The **Project Overview** screen shows your projects as cards with their status
  and metrics.

### Creating projects

- **New Project** — clone from a Git URL or point to a project folder. Pasting a
  GitHub issue URL will resolve to the repository automatically.
- **Delete a project** from the project settings *Danger Zone*.
